title: Elazar ben Charsom, the High Priest
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: According to the Rambam in his Introduction to Zera’im, he lived in the time of Antigenos, but Hyman says, “We have found no source at all for this,” for according to the narratives of Yosippon, after Shimon HaTzaddik came Elazar his brother, after him Menashe his uncle, and after him Shimon HaTzaddik’s son named Chonyo, as High Priests — unless, Hyman says, we say that he was a serving Kohen in Antigenos’s time, as we explained in the entry Shimon HaTzaddik. In Yoma 9a it is mentioned that he was High Priest for eleven years, and there, at 35b, it is related that his mother made him a tunic worth twenty thousand [dinars], and his fellow priests did not let him wear it because he looked naked in it. It is related of him there that his father left him great wealth, and he did not benefit from his wealth; he would carry a sack of flour on his shoulders and go from city to city to study Torah. Once his servants found him and pressed him into forced labor, for they did not recognize him. And where he is mentioned as Rabbi Elazar B-Ch, Hyman calls this a habit of language, for in his time they were not yet called “Rabbi.” Likewise in Kiddushin 49b he is mentioned as an example of great wealth. They said in Yoma there: “R-A ben Charsim makes the wealthy answerable.”

notes.text: The supplied משתי שיבוא is understood as two myriads; saved Davidson Yoma35b specifies twenty thousand dinars, not maneh, so the former bracketed monetary unit is corrected. ויסופר אליו is read as עליו. Hyman finds no source for the Rambam’s Antigenos placement and offers a possible reconciliation; that chronology question stays held rather than silently settled.

Thus the inherited bracketed [dinars] remains an explanatory unit, not a word explicitly present in Hyman's Hebrew; the old [maneh] and Fable keep-note endorsement remain archived rather than automatically accepted. The explicit full רבי in the discussion of Rabbi Elazar remains; its B-Ch patronymic siglum is kept literal rather than silently resolved. The final R-A ben Charsim stays abbreviated and preserves חרסים beside heading חרסום/Charsom; the local full title in the tunic scalar does not transfer to that final quotation. In the fourth chapter of his Introduction to the Mishnah, Rambam groups Antigonos of Sokho and Rabbi Elazar ben Charsom together. He gives no dates of office. In his entry on Shimon HaTzaddik (vol. III, pp. 1223–1224), Hyman attributes that succession to Josephus’s Antiquities and distinguishes serving in the Temple from leading the people or heading the Sanhedrin. The succession appears in Antiquities 12.43 and 12.157–158. The present entry cites Yosippon. The consulted print of Yosippon, chapter 17, names Eleazar the priest in Ptolemy’s translation story, alongside a separate reference to the high priest in Jerusalem. The exact text Hyman used for the succession under the name Yosippon remains unverified.

In the consulted Yoma 9a, eleven years is introduced as an alternative tradition. At Yoma 35b, Elazar’s example holds the wealthy answerable for neglecting Torah study. The consulted Bavli gives Rabbi Elazar ben Charsom, and Hyman’s printed quotation has חרסום, beside חרסים in the supplied text. Hyman’s printed story also has כתונת (tunic), משתי ריבוא (two myriads) and ויסופר עליו (it is told of him).
